scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A flowing ribbon of golden light curves through a brilliant center, surrounded by layered blue and ochre watercolor clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative watercolor uses a flowing current within one radiance to evoke John 1:1: the Word was in the beginning, was with God, and was God. The image is a metaphor, not a literal depiction. The English wording follows the verse's Berean Interlinear token glosses, identified as uncurated in the source.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A robed man sits among blue and golden clouds, looking toward brilliant light in a star-filled expanse.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the Word, referred to as 'He' in John 1:2, being with God in the beginning. The figure and light are symbolic, not a literal depiction. The verse's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An unlettered parchment scroll rests within warm golden radiance amid deep blue watercolor clouds and stars.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: A symbolic meditation on John 1:2: the Word was with God in the beginning. The scroll recalls the Word without depicting Jesus as a person. It is an illustration, not a claim that the Word is a created object or that this scene shows His pre-incarnation appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor landscape at sunrise with stars, mountains, a river, an olive tree, wildflowers, birds, and a doe with her fawn.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imagined scene: light joining a landscape full of living things evokes John 1:3's claim that all things came into being through the Word and that nothing that came into being did so without Him. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, as identified in the lesson.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among men, women, and children in a flower-filled landscape. Golden light surrounds Him, and a young leafy tree grows beside Him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 1:4: the light around Christ and the people evokes the verse's image of life in Him as the light of humanity. The token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An oil lamp glows on a stone ledge beneath an olive tree, overlooking a moonlit valley and village at night.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses a lamp shining amid the night to evoke John 1:5: the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it. The relationship follows the verse's uncurated Berean Interlinear token glosses; the scene is a visual metaphor, not a depicted event from the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a rough brown garment walks with a staff along a rocky path through sunlit hills, with a settlement and winding river in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene of John setting out evokes John 1:6, which introduces a man named John sent from God. The landscape, lighting, journey and appearance are artistic choices rather than details supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John, wearing a rough robe and holding a staff, gestures toward a golden dawn while a small gathering listens on a rocky hillside overlooking a valley and water.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of John bearing witness concerning the Light, so that all might believe through him, in John 1:7. The dawn symbolizes the Light; the specific landscape and gathering are artistic choices. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist gestures toward a golden sunrise over a river as a small group listens, in a warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined riverbank scene uses the sunrise to picture John bearing witness to the Light, while he himself is not the Light. The riverbank and dawn are artistic choices, not details asserted by John 1:8. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Golden dawn light spreads over an ancient hillside village, illuminating a woman and child, a man with a basket of bread, a woman with a water jar, and an elderly man with a staff.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined dawn scene represents John 1:9's true light illuminating people in the world; the village and its inhabitants are artistic details, not a historical event described in the verse. The English token glosses in the source are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks through a sunlit village market as people tend their work and pass by, with animals, trees and distant hills around them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:10: the Berean Interlinear token glosses describe Him as being in the world, the world as coming into being through Him, and the world as not knowing Him. The village, people, activities and shared light are artistic choices rather than details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with one hand extended outside a stone village home as three people at the doorway turn or withdraw inside.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:11, in which the Word comes to His own and His own do not receive Him. The doorway, people, and moment are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands with open arms beside a sunlit stone doorway as a group of women, men, and a child reach toward Him in a watercolor village landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests Jesus welcoming those who receive Him and believe in His name, whom He gives authority to become children of God. The encounter and doorway are visual metaphors, not events stated in the verse. The source's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five people, including two children and an elderly man, sit together in a sunlit garden and look upward as green shoots rise among stones in the foreground.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined garden scene uses the light and fresh shoots as symbols of life from God, evoking John 1:13's contrast between being born of God and birth from blood or human will. The people and garden are artistic choices, not events described in the verse. The English token glosses in the source are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit village, Jesus sits beneath a woven shelter, welcoming a group of men, women, and a child who look toward him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering evokes John 1:14's Word made flesh dwelling among people and the glory of the only begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. The verse does not describe this particular gathering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John, wearing a rough brown garment, stretches out his arm toward Jesus approaching along a riverside path while listeners watch in warm dawn light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative riverside scene pictures John bearing witness to Jesus, who comes after him yet has precedence because he was before John. The setting, listeners, and depicted moment are artistic details. The English token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear, not an approved Global Bible Tools translation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A warm watercolor scene shows Jesus beside a flowing spring, with men, women, and children gathering water in cups and cupped hands. Golden fields, a village, and hills lie beyond them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the flowing spring and the people receiving its water to picture John 1:16's fullness and grace for grace, following the verse's Berean Interlinear token glosses. The verse does not describe a literal spring or this event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree with open hands, teaching a group in a sunlit countryside while Moses stands beside him holding two blank stone tablets.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene places Moses and Jesus together to reflect John 1:17: the law was given through Moses, and grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. Their meeting here is symbolic. The English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, as identified in the chapter data.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits beneath a tree near a sunlit lake, one hand on his chest and the other open toward a small group of attentive listeners.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering evokes John 1:18: no one has seen God, and the only begotten God, close to the Father, has made Him known. The verse does not describe this gathering, landscape, or gesture. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed visitors face John on a stony riverbank. One visitor gestures with an open hand while John, dressed in rough clothing and holding a staff, listens. Reeds, water, distant hills, and hillside buildings surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the priests and Levites sent from Jerusalem to ask John who he is in John 1:19. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John, in rough clothing, touches his chest and gestures openly toward two listening men beside a reed-lined river, with hills in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John openly confessing that he is not the Christ in John 1:20. The questioners and Jordan setting draw on the surrounding passage; the gestures and appearance are artistic choices. The chapter identifies the English token glosses as Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist in a rough brown robe raises both hands as two robed men question him beside a sunlit river, with reeds and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 1:21, where John answers that he is neither Elijah nor the prophet. The setting, gestures, and clothing are artistic interpretation; the verse's English token glosses come from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist listens beside the Jordan as a robed messenger gestures toward him and two other men watch, with reeds and sunlit hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the messengers asking John who he is and what he says about himself so they can answer those who sent them. The verse's word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing a rough brown garment and holding a staff, calls out and gestures toward a straight path through a sunlit, rocky wilderness.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:23, where John describes himself as a voice crying in the wilderness and calls for the Lord's way to be made straight, as Isaiah the prophet said. The landscape, staff, gesture, and visible path are artistic choices; the verse does not describe this pictured moment or a literal road. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Several robed men stand together and speak with John, who holds a staff, on the rocky, reed-lined bank of a river.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 1:24, which identifies those sent as being from the Pharisees. The surrounding passage places their exchange with John beyond the Jordan; the figures, gestures and landscape are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear and are not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit riverbank, three robed men question John the Baptist; one gestures with an open hand as John listens, with reeds, water, and hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene inspired by John 1:25, in which they ask John why he baptizes if he is not the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic interpretations. The chapter's English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John, wearing a rough brown garment, speaks with an open hand to a gathered crowd beside a sunlit river, with trees, hills and a village beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows John speaking beside water to listeners, evoking his words that he baptizes with water and that someone they do not know stands among them. The setting and individual appearances are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, in a rough brown garment, gestures toward an approaching robed man in fastened sandals as listeners watch beside a sunlit river.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene evokes John 1:27, where John says he is not worthy to untie the sandal strap of the one coming after him. The verse does not describe this particular arrangement or say that John untied the sandal.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John, in a rough brown garment, supports an unnamed man in the Jordan as five people watch from a reed-lined bank, with hills and a small settlement in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John baptizing near Bethany across the Jordan, the place described in John 1:28. The person being baptized, the onlookers, and the landscape are artistic details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist holds a staff and gestures toward Jesus as He approaches along a sunlit riverbank, with a white lamb beside Jesus.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:29, in which John sees Jesus coming and identifies Him as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. The riverside setting, staff, and accompanying lamb are artistic choices, not details stated in this verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, dressed in a rough brown garment, gestures toward Jesus beside a river while listeners watch in warm golden light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John identifying Jesus as the man who comes after him yet has precedence because he was before him. The riverside setting and golden light are artistic choices.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing a rough brown garment, supports a wet man in the Jordan River as Jesus stands among onlookers on the riverbank.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene connects John’s testimony that he did not know Jesus with his coming to baptize in water so Jesus might be revealed to Israel. The pictured moment and arrangement are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John gestures on a rocky riverbank as Jesus stands in the water with a white dove resting on his shoulder beneath a beam of light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John's testimony that he saw the Spirit descend from heaven like a dove and remain upon Jesus.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist and Jesus stand in the Jordan as John holds Jesus' hands and a white dove settles on Jesus' shoulder; reeds and sunlit hills surround the river.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 1:33, where John recounts being sent to baptize with water and the sign of the Spirit descending and remaining on the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit. The dove draws on the surrounding account in John 1:32; the scene's appearance is an artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, dressed in a rough brown garment, gestures toward Jesus as a group listens beside a river, with reeds and sunlit hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative riverside scene depicts John the Baptist bearing witness to what he has seen: that Jesus is the Son of God, as in John 1:34. The setting and listeners are artistic details. The verse wording follows the chapter's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing a coarse brown garment, holds a staff and gestures while standing with two robed disciples on a rocky riverbank.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:35, in which John was standing again with two of his disciples on the next day. The riverbank, appearances, clothing, staff, and gestures are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist gestures toward Jesus walking beside a river as two disciples watch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative rendering of John 1:36, where John looks at Jesus walking and calls him the Lamb of God; the two disciples are mentioned in the preceding verse. The riverbank and visual details are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist gestures toward Jesus as two disciples follow Him along a sunlit riverside path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:37, in which two disciples hear John speaking and follow Jesus. The riverside path, gestures, clothing, and landscape are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit country path, Jesus turns toward two men following Him and extends an open hand as they look at Him; a tree, wildflowers, distant hills and a village surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 1:38, when Jesus turns toward those following Him, asks what they seek, and they address Him as Rabbi, meaning Teacher, and ask where He is staying. The landscape and appearances are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward the open doorway of a stone dwelling as two disciples approach in warm afternoon light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:39, where Jesus invites the two disciples to come and see where He is staying; they come and remain with Him that day, and the verse says it was about the tenth hour. The dwelling, setting, clothing and gestures are artistic choices. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus walks along a sunlit path ahead of two disciples as John the Baptist points toward him from behind them; hills, water, and a village lie in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 1:40, which identifies Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, as one of the two who heard John and followed Jesus. The landscape, appearances, and particular moment are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone village, Andrew gestures eagerly while speaking to Simon, who listens with his hands against his chest.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Andrew finding his brother Simon and telling him that they have found the Messiah, called Christ in John 1:41. The setting, expressions, and gestures are artistic choices. The verse relationship follows the Berean Interlinear word glosses identified in the source file.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Andrew stands just behind Simon with a hand on his shoulder, while Jesus faces Simon and speaks with open hands on a sunny path among hills and trees.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 1:42: Andrew brings Simon to Jesus, and Jesus looks at Simon and tells him he will be called Cephas, interpreted as Peter. Andrew is identified in the preceding verses. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The English word glosses in the chapter are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus extends an open hand toward Philip on a sunlit path, with olive trees, hills, a village, and water in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:43, where Jesus intends to go to Galilee, finds Philip, and says to him, 'Follow me.' The road, gestures, and landscape are artistic choices rather than details supplied by the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men in robes stand on a rocky path above a lakeside town; one gestures toward the clustered stone houses and boats along the shore.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative view of Bethsaida, which John 1:44 identifies as Philip's hometown and the city of Andrew and Peter. The verse does not describe the pictured gathering.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: On a sunlit hillside path, a man holding a rolled scroll speaks with an open hand to another man, who listens thoughtfully; olive trees, stone walls, water, and a village fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 1:45, in which Philip finds Nathanael and says they have found Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth, the one Moses wrote of in the Law and the prophets also wrote of. The landscape, appearances, gestures, and scroll are artistic choices. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Nathanael, in earth-toned robes, raises a questioning hand as Philip, in a blue cloak, gestures invitingly toward a path through sunlit hills, with a village in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 1:46, in which Nathanael asks whether anything good can come from Nazareth and Philip replies, 'Come and see.' Their appearances, gestures, and setting are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward Nathanael as he approaches along a sunlit path among olive trees and stone walls, with hills and a village in the distance.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts Jesus seeing Nathanael approach and speaking of him as a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with a surprised Nathanael beside a fruiting fig tree, amid sunlit hills, stone walls, and a distant village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This scene imaginatively places Jesus and Nathanael's conversation beside a fig tree. In John 1:48, Jesus says He saw Nathanael under a fig tree before Philip called him; the location of their conversation is not specified. The supplied English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Beneath a fig tree, Nathanael sits facing Jesus, touching his chest and gesturing toward him as he speaks. A sunlit village and hills lie beyond them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Nathanael's answer to Jesus in John 1:49, when he addresses him as Rabbi, Son of God, and King of Israel. The setting and gestures are artistic choices. The English word glosses used for the interpretation come from the Berean Interlinear layer.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures as He speaks to Nathanael, who listens with a hand on his chest; both sit beneath a fruiting fig tree overlooking sunlit hills and a village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus speaking to Nathanael after saying He saw him under the fig tree and promising that he would see greater things. The seated figures and setting are artistic choices. The English token glosses used for this scene are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, identified in the lesson as uncurated and not GBT-approved.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands among listeners on a rocky hillside, looking up at angels ascending and descending in golden light beneath an opening in the clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visualization of Jesus' promise in John 1:51 that His hearers will see heaven opened and God's angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man. The hillside, listeners, and visible vision are artistic choices rather than details supplied by the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.
